hypothesis: A cap of 3 makes saving impossible at the decisive moment: a prepared responder needs 2 Prestige for fee plus boost, leaving no room to also hold a support purchase, and counterleader and prestige_farmer waste 0.65 and 0.46 Prestige per game at the cap (baseline holdout). A cap of 4 lets a planner bank fee plus boost plus one support, so banking Prestige for the endgame becomes a real alternative to spending it immediately instead of a forced conversion.
prediction: Prestige wasted at cap falls by at least half; responder affordability rises above 0.80 and contest offerings do not fall; prestige_farmer and early_support win shares move toward a quarter; first-challenger win share stays within five points of baseline; draws and median rounds stay within the frozen guards.
refutation_evidence: Wasted-at-cap does not fall by half; or cancellations per game rise (a richer field buying more boosts would show the banking plan merely purchases more churn); or the first challenger's share rises past baseline plus five points; or any mechanical or counterplay gate fails on either suite.
